astro.notes: matched=false for all six because the official docs were unreachable (browser 401s), not because of a doc/behavior mismatch. Every probe produced a build-backed measurement.

docusaurus.notes: matched=false for all six because the official docs site could not be loaded, not because of a doc/behavior mismatch. Every probe produced a build-backed measurement.

eleventy.notes: P1 (missing order sorts last, contradicting the docs' 'defaults to 0') and P3 (ties break by collection order, docs silent) revealed rules beyond or against the docs.

hugo.notes: matched=false for all six because the official docs could not be loaded, not because of a doc/behavior mismatch. Every probe produced a build-backed measurement.

jekyll.notes: All six probes agreed with the just-the-docs documentation (14 verbatim quotes collected). The P3 tie is documented as unstable, so its outcome is unpredictable in principle rather than unresolved.

mkdocs.notes: matched=false for all six because the official docs could not be loaded, not because of a doc/behavior mismatch. Every probe produced a build-backed measurement against the explicit-nav starter.

nuxt.notes: matched=false for all six because the official docs could not be loaded. All placement claims are against a probe harness serializing queryCollectionNavigation, since the starter renders no navigation markup.

vitepress.notes: All six probes agreed with the official package documentation (verbatim JSDoc quotes; vitepress.dev itself was unreachable). P3 has no tie concept in the default theme; the analogue probe confirmed config-array order.

note_on_matched_false: For astro, docusaurus, hugo, mkdocs, and nuxt, matched_documented_rule=false means 'no documented rule could be consulted because the docs were unreachable in this environment', NOT 'the behavior contradicted the docs'. The two meanings are kept distinct in each probe JSON's notes.
